slice.question: Does Sigstore's documented identity-monitoring path provide deletion-surviving enumeration from a stable GitHub repository/workflow identity without a pre-retained artifact digest, and can a release tag or release predicate be filtered from the discovered signed record while preserving the Phase-1 zero-quota/zero-cost/no-external-executor constraints?

sources.title: Threat Model - Sigstore
sources.observed: Sigstore documents rekor-monitor as a log monitor that can detect occurrences of an identity and states current identity monitoring supports hashedrekord entries with exact identity matching.

sources.title: sigstore/rekor-monitor README
sources.observed: The monitor accepts startIndex/endIndex ranges, matches certificate SAN identities for hashedrekord entries, can match Fulcio OID extensions including build-signer-uri and source-repository-uri, and gives an exact build-signer-uri example containing @refs/tags/v1.4.0. The documented reusable deployment uses GitHub Actions and retained workflow artifacts, and the default monitor starts from the latest checkpoint; historical entries require a separate log query.

sources.title: OIDC Usage in Fulcio - Sigstore
sources.observed: For GitHub Actions, Fulcio places job_workflow_ref in the certificate SAN URI and extracts the ref claim into custom OID fields. The documented certificate identity therefore binds repository/workflow and ref, allowing a tag ref to be distinguished when the signer ran from refs/tags/<tag>.

sources.title: Rekor public log info endpoint
sources.observed: A direct public read from scheduled Chat returned Rekor log metadata without authentication, including active treeSize 2264097833, confirming that at least log-head metadata is Chat-readable without a hosted runner, secret, paid service, or finite monthly credit.

reasoning: The previous r279 blocker was specifically the absence of a repository/tag discovery key. Official Sigstore documentation now establishes a different discovery primitive: scan a Rekor index range and filter returned hashedrekord certificates by stable GitHub workflow identity rather than first knowing the artifact digest.

For GitHub Actions signatures, the Fulcio certificate identity contains the workflow reference and the ref claim is also represented in certificate metadata. rekor-monitor explicitly demonstrates build-signer-uri matching on a refs/tags/v1.4.0 value, so a tag can be filtered for supported hashedrekord entries after enumeration without an artifact digest.

This does not establish a GitHub release predicate filter. Predicate type is not shown as an identity-monitor key, and it is not established that GitHub automatic immutable-release attestations use the supported hashedrekord path with a tag-bearing Fulcio certificate. Therefore the original release-attestation deletion witness is not closed.

The documented rekor-monitor deployment itself is not Phase-1 acceptable because it consumes GitHub Actions execution and retained artifacts. A standalone algorithm exists, but direct scheduled-Chat retrieval/parsing of bounded Rekor entry ranges has not yet been proven in this role; only the public log-head read was directly demonstrated here.

A forward monitor also needs a monotonic checkpoint/start index to avoid rescanning the full log. That state is generic rather than artifact-specific, but it remains retained state and therefore cannot be silently treated as eliminated under the current fail-closed contract.
slice.tested_scope: Official public Sigstore documentation and the unauthenticated Rekor public log-info endpoint only. No O, downstream, other worker state/config/receipt, legacy research, shared ledger, repository release/admin mutation, local CLI execution, GitHub Actions execution, webhook/external storage, hosted compute/storage, external executor, manual witness, finite monthly/trial/paid quota consumption, added cost, scheduler mutation, retry, wait/poll, or second leaf.

frontier: Preserve r273 single-ref immutable transaction-record plus force=false ref-update design as the current Chat-callable baseline.
r276 rejected GitHub Events API as a durable monotonic witness because visibility is bounded and not real-time.
r277 rejected immutable releases alone because release deletion lacks a normal public deletion-tombstone lookup.
r278 established promising independent public retention through Sigstore/Rekor but left deletion-surviving discovery-key derivation unresolved.
r279 falsified direct repository-plus-tag lookup through GitHub attestation REST and normal Rekor get/search keys without retained identifiers.

r280 establishes a distinct forward discovery primitive for supported hashedrekord signatures: enumerate Rekor log-index ranges and filter Fulcio SAN/OID identity, including tag-bearing build-signer-uri values. It remains fail-closed because the provided deployment uses hosted Actions/artifacts, direct Chat entry-range retrieval is unproven, the relevant automatic release-attestation entry type is unverified, and practical forward monitoring retains a generic log-index checkpoint.
